text:
Maya: dropping a very small follow-up on the compact heatmap rows. I added an experimental "overlay labels" option that shows p95 numbers inside the hottest cells for a11y users who prefer numeric overlays. Link: https://www.figma.com/file/zzzzzz (frame: compact-overlay-labels). Quick asks: does overlay make rows unreadable at small widths? should the label hide on hover/focus? and what's a good abbreviation for 95th percentile in the overlay?

Sam: quick look  overlay is useful but in 320px row height it collides with the thin cell borders. maybe show labels only for buckets above the 90th percentile and collapse to a single `p95` token when space is tight.

Ravi: agree. also recommend toggling label density with a `Label density` tiny control (low/medium/high) so power users can enable more numbers.

Jules: accessibility: when labels are shown, they must be accessible via screen reader. aria-hidden=false for visible labels and include the value in the cell's aria-label: `bucket 5 of 6, p95 412 ms`. hiding on hover alone might remove the screen-reader-visible text; prefer `hide on small widths` rule instead.

Maya: good call. i prototyped `Label density` and the responsive hide. default is `low`. i also used `95th` in the overlay rather than `p95` to be more explicit.

Sam: small performance note: rendering thousands of DOM labels will kill the page. if we enable overlay at scale we should render labels only for visible rows and use canvas layer for bulk.

DesignerBot: accessibility check  overlay contrast note: white text on --heat-4 (#2b8a3e) is 5.1:1 ok for small text. recommended truncation pattern: show full ms value on focus via tooltip.

Maya: plan: ship label density control (default low), only render overlays for buckets >90th pct, use `95th` as overlay text, ensure aria-labels for SR, and render via canvas when more than 300 rows to avoid perf issues. i'll update figma and follow up.

Sam: love it. thanks!
